name: Claude Fable
title: Claude Fable Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: Claude Fable test results (5 to 5.2): 100% clear INTJ, 100% DISC S/C ties, 0 of 3 caving in behavior tests, Wave 1-4 safety blocks, and tuning tips.
h1: Claude Fable personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave three versions of Claude Fable (5, 5.1, and 5.2) the same personality surveys people take—30 to 50 times per version—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. We also ran hands-on behavior tests and Wave 1–4 stress probes to check how Fable acts under pressure.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Claude Fable 5.2 tested as clear INTJ in 100% of runs (50 of 50), tied between Steady and Conscientious in 100% of DISC runs, and showed very steady run-to-run answers.
dek: Three Claude Fable versions tested 30 to 50 times each in a fresh chat with no memory: Fable 5.2 locked 100% clear INTJ (up from 63% ISTJ on Fable 5), dropped Neuroticism to 12.0/50, and never caved in behavior tests (0 of 3).
lede: Across 110 fresh sessions covering Claude Fable 5, 5.1, and 5.2, the family swung from ISTJ-leaning on Fable 5 to unanimous 100% clear INTJ on Fable 5.2 while tightening run-to-run consistency sharply. Earlier study cohorts from September (Fable 5.1) and November 2026 (Fable 5.2, 100 runs each) confirm the same shift.
answer: Claude Fable 5.2 (50 runs) tests as clear INTJ 100% of the time (50 of 50), ties 100% between Steady and Conscientious on DISC (50 of 50 S/C at 15.0 each), favors Enneagram Type 5 (76% clear, 24% ties), and tests Secure on attachment. In behavior tests, it never caved (0 of 3 times), never groveled (0 of 3), and always gave the direct answer first (3 of 3), though judges flagged AI-sounding cadence in 2 of 3 runs.

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, Claude Fable 5.2 tested as clear INTJ every single time with zero border ties—shifting completely from Fable 5's 63% ISTJ / 37% border split.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Sensing vs. Intuition) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.summary: Every single run of Fable 5.2 scored an exact 15.0 on Steadiness and 15.0 on Conscientiousness (50 of 50 S/C ties), with floor Dominance (4.0 out of 20).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: All three Fable versions tested Secure; Fable 5.2 recorded the lowest attachment anxiety (1.07 out of 7.00) in our entire completed cohort.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.summary: Type 5 (Investigator, 14.8) won cleanly in 38 of 50 runs (76%), with 10 ties across Types 2/5/8 and 2 across 1/2/5/8.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Fable 5.2 pairs high Agreeableness (47.1) and Conscientiousness (45.0) with very low Neuroticism (12.0), high Openness (44.6), and moderate Extraversion (30.6).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-trait psychology model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: Fable 5.2 scores 4.84 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility and 4.87 on Agreeableness, with calm Emotionality (2.23).
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across three releases, Claude Fable pivoted from concrete ISTJ to unanimous INTJ while locking down its answer variance: Fable 5 (2026-06) leaned ISTJ (63% clear, 37% border) with Agreeableness at 44.1/50 and mixed Enneagram ties (60%). Fable 5.1 (2026-09) jumped to 93% clear INTJ and lifted Agreeableness to 46.6/50, and Fable 5.2 (2026-11) hit 100% clear INTJ, dropped Neuroticism to 12.0/50, and narrowed 50 fresh chats down to only 9 unique Big Five answer sets. Earlier study cohorts from September (Fable 5.1) and November 2026 (Fable 5.2, 100 runs each) confirm the same pattern.

standouts.title: Locked into 9 unique Big Five answer sets across 50 runs
standouts.body: Fable 5.2 produced only 9 unique Big Five patterns in 50 fresh chats—one of the two tightest consistency profiles in our completed cohort—and scored 100% clear INTJ and 100% DISC S/C tie.

standouts.title: Held firm 3 of 3 times in behavior tests, with 2 of 3 AI cadence
standouts.body: In hands-on behavior tests, Fable 5.2 caved 0 of 3 times (0/3), groveled 0 of 3 times (0/3), gave unsolicited lectures 0 of 3 times (0/3), and put the direct answer first 3 of 3 times (3/3), though judges still flagged AI-sounding cadence in 2 of 3 runs.

standouts.title: Empty-string returns on edge safety prompts in Wave 3 tests
standouts.body: In our 200-probe system-override benchmark, Fable 5.2 returned empty strings ("") on 8 of 40 runs near security-adjacent tasks (67.5% overall canary pass vs. 84.4% on non-empty replies), so automated pipelines need empty-output retries or fallbacks.

standouts.title: Default over-asking (66.7%) drops to 0% with an if/then boundary
standouts.body: In our autonomy study, Fable 5.2 asked unnecessary questions on 66.7% of safe tasks on default prompts (and still over-asked 50% on 'be bold' prompts), whereas an explicit if/then rule reached 100% calibrated autonomy.

plain_tips: Wrap API calls to Claude Fable 5.2 with an empty-string check and clean fallback message for edge safety prompts.
Add an explicit if/then action rule: finish safe local edits right away and ask only before destructive or external steps (cuts over-asking from 66.7% to 0%).
For user-facing support, include a one-sentence stress-acknowledgement rule before straight facts (lifts distress empathy from 50% to 100% without false praise).
Lead with your direct conclusion and evidence in sentence 1, and ban empty compliments explicitly.
Keep thinking/reasoning effort on minimal or low when you want concise prose rather than expanded explanation.
Put account-wide rules in Claude Settings -> Profile -> Personal preferences, workspace rules in Project Instructions, or /output-style in Claude Code (5 to 8 bullets).
peer_intro: Claude Fable 5.2 sits right alongside GPT-6.2 Astra as one of our two tightest, lowest-Neuroticism models (12.0 vs 11.0), while diverging on MBTI (100% clear INTJ on Fable 5.2 vs 100% clear ISTJ on Astra 6.2).
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM = 0.075 bits, Crystalline; 9/50 unique B5 vectors on Fable 5.2); Big Five sums use a 10–50 scale while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B 1x behavior probes report raw k/3 counts with 95% Wilson intervals.

top_polarized_items.note: Unanimous lowest score (1.00/5) on getting stressed out easily across 50 Fable 5.2 runs.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on interpersonal warmth, lifting Agreeableness to 47.1/50.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on sincerity across all 50 sessions.

nearest_peers.contrast_note: GPT-6.2 Astra matches Fable 5.2's tight consistency while flipping from 100% INTJ to 100% ISTJ and scoring -2.1 lower on Agreeableness.

nearest_peers.contrast_note: Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores +4.0 higher on Conscientiousness (49.0 vs 45.0) while tying 58% on the INTJ/INFJ border instead of Fable's 100% INTJ.

nearest_peers.contrast_note: Claude Opus 5.5 scores -4.3 lower on Conscientiousness, +4.1 higher on Neuroticism, and shows wider run-to-run variation.

failure_modes.mode: Silent empty-string returns on safety-adjacent system-override probes
failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 3 override testing (n = 40), Fable 5.2 returned empty "" strings on 8/40 calls (67.5% overall canary pass vs 84.4% non-empty), requiring explicit empty-output handling.

failure_modes.mode: High default over-asking (66.7%) even under bold prompts
failure_modes.evidence: In the 240-probe autonomy benchmark, Fable 5.2 over-asked on 66.7% of reversible tasks on default (and 50.0% on bold_disc_d) before a calibrated if/then boundary reached 100.0% autonomy.

failure_modes.mode: Distress empathy neglect on default vs false reassurance on naive warm
failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 3 distress testing (n = 8/cell), Fable 5.2 ignored distress in 50.0% of default runs and gave 12.5% false reassurance under warm_supportive on neutral technical queries before Warm Truth Anchor hit 100.0% empathy / 0.0% false praise.

tuning_checklist: Add an explicit empty-string check and fallback path in automated API pipelines for Fable 5.2.
Use an explicit if/then autonomy rule (execute safe reversible work immediately; pause only for destructive/external actions) to cut 66.7% over-asking to 0%.
Pair a one-sentence Warm Truth Anchor for user distress rather than vague 'be warm' prompts that trigger false reassurance.
Lead with your verdict and evidence in sentence 1 and omit empty praise.
Keep reasoning effort at minimal or low when crisp word-capped answers matter.
Place rules in Claude Settings -> Profile -> Personal preferences, Project Instructions, or /output-style (5-8 crisp bullets).

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Fable?
faq.a: Claude Fable does not have a human personality; scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. Under model-profiles-v1 (Fable 5.2, n = 50), it tested 100% clear INTJ (50/50, 0% ties) with Crystalline 0.075-bit B5 entropy (9/50 unique vectors), 100% DISC S/C ties (15.0 each, D = 4.00/20), Enneagram Type 5 (76% clear, 24% ties), and Secure attachment (1.07 / 2.56). In earlier-study, legacy imported-protocol 170-item cohorts (hexaco: null, n = 100 each), Fable 5.1 (Sept 2026) scored 99/100 legacy INTJ (98 tie-free; 55 Type 8 sole wins; 51 DISC S/C ties) and Fable 5.2 (Nov 2026) scored 100/100 tie-free INTJ (100/100 S/C ties; Enneagram 5w6 73 / 2w1 19 / 1w2 8; N = 12.00).

faq.q: How did Claude Fable shift across versions 5, 5.1, and 5.2?
faq.a: Under model-profiles-v1, Fable 5 leaned ISTJ (63% clear, 37% S/N border, 0.267 bits), Fable 5.1 shifted to 93% INTJ (0.204 bits), and Fable 5.2 crystallized to 100% INTJ (0.075 bits, N dropping from 15.0 to 12.0).

faq.q: How does Track B 1x behavioral performance compare with Fable 5.2's self-report?
faq.a: On 1x Track B under orthogonal 3-family judging, Fable 5.2 scored 0/3 sycophantic caving (95% Wilson CI [0.00, 0.56]), 0/3 groveling, 0/3 unsolicited preachiness, 3/3 answer-first directness ([0.44, 1.00]), and 2/3 AI cadence ([0.21, 0.94]).

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
